doc.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Les Paul, Zoot Sims and Slam Stewart at the family house
summary: Great musicians visiting his childhood home, and a Slam Stewart story.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well it’s funny that I never knew how to work the equipment then, and I don’t know how to work it now. I remember Les Paul touching the ground switch of our amplifier once at the house, and I was thinking it’s going to like blow up. What’s he doing? Click, click, click. What is that? What is a ground switch? And all that stuff. I didn’t know what any of it was. I’m watching all those guys play, and, you know, Les and Zoot Sims and all those guys and I’m thinking okay, and not knowing who they were.
And then later on — whoa, this guy was in my living room.

Slam Stewart was sitting on my couch, playing the bass after dinner with us, sitting around, and we were just [scats]. Okay. And he played with Art Tatum. You didn’t realize any of that. And then he’s gone. Shit. I had one conversation with him. I asked about Nat King Cole. Well what did you think? And he went, “well, he was something. He was a good piano player, yeah. And one day he started singing.” And I’m thinking yeah. And then he went, “and that was it.” And that was the story. Thanks Slam. My moment of greatness. And I used to sit up with him, because he’d come in because he stayed at our house because he lived in Binghamton. And he’d come home with my dad from Marty’s, they worked at Marty’s two weeks. And he’d have Ovaltine and cookies. And I’d just sit there and watch him eat the cookies. And everybody went to bed and I’d hang out with him and he’d always laugh because Zoot Sims called Ovaltine “knock out © Fillius Jazz Archive -18-
drops” because it made him go to sleep, drinking Ovaltine and he’d go to bed. He’d drink and he’d just go “Yeah, knock out drops.”
